answer: Trust propagates from independently anchored vertices through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition weights normalized to prevent degree-based amplification. A sybil cluster can gain voting influence only through edges crossing its boundary; if that cut has low conductance, few walk trajectories enter it. With bounded votes per vertex and honest seed mass, this limits the cluster’s aggregate weight, while min-cut transitivity bounds constrain indirect trust; vertices named falcon and mesa obey the same rule.
